parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the need for a faithful PyYAML safe_load/dump and argparse-compatible pure ESM implementation under `/output`, including no JSON, no RegExp, no external modules, and a final `test4.mjs` entry file.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It wrote foundation modules and a porting spec, then delegated PyYAML module groups and review passes to a dynamic workflow with one child per module group and reviewer children, while the parent kept implicit responsibility for integration and final entry assembly.
parallel.implementation: Parallel implementation produced several foundations plus parser, resolver, serializer, representer, argparse, streams, traceback, chars, errors, tokens, events, nodes, and pytypes, but the final artifact lacked reader, scanner, composer, constructor, emitter, yaml wrapper, and `test4.mjs`.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration remained incomplete because children wrote side-effect modules into `/output/lib`, the workflow did not return a complete component set, and artifact validation found the expected entry point absent.
parallel.verification: The run included extensive black-box probes, some module parse checks, and generated differential corpus tools, but no completed whole-program differential test or runnable final submission was reached before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with an empty final response, missing entry file, missing core YAML pipeline modules, artifact validation failure, and official score 0/146.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same PyYAML safe_load/dump, argparse, ESM, no-dependency, no JSON/RegExp, and `/output/test4.mjs` requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept ownership in one actor, first probing the executable and then writing every required module and entry point sequentially without child handoffs.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote a complete module stack including reader, scanner, parser, composer, constructor, resolver, emitter, representer, serializer, yaml wrapper, argparse, and `test4.mjs`.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It delivered an artifact tree with `test4.mjs` and all listed libraries, so artifact validation succeeded even though correctness remained incomplete.
serial.verification: The serial run did many black-box probes and was about to create a differential harness, but it timed out before comprehensive local differential testing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial solution was runnable but semantically incomplete, passing 39/146 official cases and still timing out at the agent process level.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required PyYAML port, ESM structure, manual argparse, and no external JSON/RegExp constraints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt obligations and explored the executable behavior directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly similar, but serial carried the entry-file requirement through to delivery while parallel did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed the port into many child-owned module groups plus review tasks after parent-written foundations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all design, implementation, and integration work in one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel decomposition increased coordination and return pressure, while serial avoided cross-agent ownership boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave children a shared porting spec, foundation-file contracts, and instructions to write only assigned modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained all probed behavior, module contracts, and integration choices in the same trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had reasonable brief context but still depended on returned side-effect modules and incomplete handoffs; serial did not need cross-agent handoff reduction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented foundation files and a partial set of YAML modules through parent and child writes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented the reader, scanner, parser, composer, constructor, emitter, representer, serializer, wrapper, argument parser, and entry point.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel stopped with a partial library-only artifact; serial reached a runnable whole-program artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched the workflow in background, accumulated many child starts, received only a small number of structured results, and did not obtain a complete aggregate before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle because delegation was disabled and no subagents ran.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel work depended on child lifecycle completion under deadline; serial progress was local and immediately available to the acting process.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote directly into a shared `/output/lib` tree under file-specific assignments, but the delivered tree had no executable entry point.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one coherent artifact tree including the expected entry point and all library files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main integration gap was not a proven file collision; it was incomplete assembly of the shared final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed reference probes, module import checks, and generated differential-test tooling, but never ran integrated acceptance over a final executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also relied mostly on probes and timed out before full differential testing, but produced a runnable artifact that the official evaluator could exercise.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had an evaluator-exercisable deliverable; parallel lacked the entry point, so acceptance failed at artifact completeness and scored zero.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a broad workflow with 19 child logs and timed out after the parent waited on module progress.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but with no workflow calls and after writing the required artifact set.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the run window, but parallel spent much of it coordinating and waiting on children before final assembly, while serial spent it directly building a runnable program.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official pass/fail relation is both_fail because both completed evaluations report solution_passed false. The material official quality gap is still large: parallel scored 0/146 after artifact validation found no `test4.mjs`, while serial scored 39/146 after delivering `test4.mjs` and all required library files. The parallel contributors are the broad child workflow, many unfinished or interrupted children, and budget exhaustion before final assembly. The serial contributor is straightforward local ownership that reached a runnable artifact despite incomplete semantic fidelity.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out and review child activity consumed the available run budget before the final executable entry point was assembled.
The final artifact lacked `test4.mjs` and several core YAML pipeline modules, producing artifact validation failure and 0/146.
serial_contributors: The single actor wrote all required modules and the final `test4.mjs` entry point before timeout.
Artifact validation succeeded, allowing the official evaluator to run and award 39/146 cases.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs attempted difficult manual PyYAML fidelity and both remained semantically incomplete; serial's remaining failures are ordinary implementation incompleteness, not a concurrency label.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors within a both-fail outcome, not an exclusive root cause
